chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, from Rib'i, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding the man to whom a will is entrusted, he said: 'When it is sent to him from a land, he is not permitted to return it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an executor receives a will but wants to return it?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the obligation of the *wasi* (executor) upon receiving the will from a distance. The ruling that he 'cannot return it' signifies that the transfer of possession is complete and binding, thereby imposing a mandatory duty to preserve and execute the bequest rather than rejecting it, which underscores the seriousness of fulfilling trusts (*amanah*) in Shia jurisprudence.
